notes: *as at the first time* gives *as at* to kĕ as one compound rendering (rule 30); the competing reading marks *at* `added`, which would leave a word the ASV wrote answering to no morpheme in a phrase where the preposition is present.
In *that time also* the ASV states nothing of the preposition's own relation, so bĕ and its assimilated article are unrepresented while the demonstrative takes the written determiner (rules 40, 41).

*would not destroy*: the ASV writes the modal and the negation as separate words, so rule 35 splits them — *would* to ʾābāh, *not* to lōʾ — and the bare infinitive has no written *to* to place (rule 52's closing sentence).
